chapter: Chicago, Lee Collins and the road
title: New Orleans as the Metropolitan City
summary: He explains Arthur Stanley's phrase and contrasts New Orleans with the black and white Southern towns where musicians had to play for two audiences.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: The late Arthur Stanley called New Orleans the Metropolitan City. And I got to understand what that means. It's not all White and Black Baptists, like you would go into Beaufort, Georgia or something, or you were going to Calverton(?), Alabama, or somewhere in Mississippi, where all the people... And there's two people -- White and Black. Because you have to always observe that when you're playing music, who you're playing for and what kind of music to play for them, and how to please and satisfy these people.
